item.title: Fluorescent probes reveal fluid-like barriers inside nuclear pores of living human cells
item.description: Our genetic material is hidden inside the nucleus of our cells, well protected by a double membrane. However, exactly how transport takes place within them has been the subject of much debate. Researchers at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (JGU), the Max Planck Institute for Biophysics (MPI-BP) in Frankfurt am Main and Wuhan University in China have now shed light on the matter. item.title: Superconducting vortices provide experimental evidence that clogging is a phase transition
item.description: Clogging is a phenomenon in which moving particles get stuck, slowing or blocking the flow, but how this transition occurs has remained experimentally unproven. Researchers from Science Tokyo studied superconducting vortices to demonstrate that clogging is a nonequilibrium phase transition. Using a two-step measurement protocol, they distinguished clogging from conventional pinning and revealed that both transitions share a critical point, offering new insights into predicting and controlling clogging across diverse systems. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Microplastics may be changing the colour of the Pacific Ocean
item.description: Research indicates that microplastics in the Great Pacific Garbage Patch may be changing ocean color. This change creates a subtle blue-green tint that satellites have detected over twenty years. Scientists analyzed how microplastics affect light scattering and absorption and compared it with natural materials. Future studies will require optical measurements from the patch for confirmation. Preventing microplastics from entering oceans is critical to reducing their impact. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
